SPECIFICATION FOR STEEL HAMMERS ( Second Revision )
1. Scope ~- Covers the requirements

n) Keying hammer. 3. Material 3.1 The hammer heads shall be manufactured from fully killed forging quality steel meeting the requirements of hardness and tests laid down in 4 and 15. Suitable examples of steel are grade T 50, r 55, T 65 or T 70 of schedule VI of IS : 1570-1961 ' Schedules for wrought steel for general engineerng practices `. 1. 9. Manufacture,

Workmanship

9.1 The hammer heads shall be cleanly forged and/or stamped in one piece. These shall be wellshaped and reasonably free from flaws, seams or other defects. All fins or flaws produced in forging or stamping shall be dressed to a reasonably level surface. 9.2 The eye shall be well-shaped a central waist. and reasonably central, and shall be drifted from both sides to leave

9.3 The striking faces and peins of hammer heads shall be finished to a reasonably smooth, bright The striking faces may be slightly convexed and chamsurface and all sharp edges shall be removed. Where any other finish is required, this shall be fered. The peino shall be well-shaped and finished. clearly stated by the purchaser in enquiry and order. 10. Preservative Treatment with an approved anti-corrosive paint,

10.1 The hammer heads shall be varnished all over or coated except the ground portion, which shall be left varnished. 11. Supply of Hammers

11.1 General requirements relating to the supply of hammers shall conform requirements for the supply of metallurgical materials ( first revision ) `. 12. Marking

to IS : 1387-1967

' General

12.1 Each hammer head shall be clearly and legibly stamped with its nominal mass and the supplier's name, initials and/or trade-mark. `fear of manufacture may also be marked when specifically required by the purchaser. 12,2 `13. IS/ Certification Packing securely packed in suitable packing cases of size convenient for bundled and secured suitably with wire, as may be specified by the hammer head shall be kept separate when packed and no package of hammer heads. Marking Details available with the Indian Standards Institution.

14.1 In order lo ascertain the conformity of the lot. the procedure for sampling inspection as given in IS : 2500 (Part I)-1973 ' Sampling inspection tables : Part I Inspection by attributes and by count of defects (first revision) ' shall be followed. For dimensions, workmanship end finish, hardness and`other tests, a single sampling plan with inspection level IV and AQL of 4 percent given in Tables 1 and 2 of IS : 2500 (Part I)-1973 shall be followed.
15. Tests

15.1 Soundness and Assembly points and edges, all hammers

Tests In order to determine shall be capable of complying with

satisfactory hardness the requirements of 15.2

of

striking

15.2 The hammer head shall be fitted with handle conforming to IS : 4953-1973. With the normal grip of the handle, six full sharp consecutive blows shall be struck with the face, pein point or edge on a rigidly supported bar of steel that complies with the material specification as laid down in 3, and that has been normalized.

15.2.1 On satisfactory completion of the test specified in 15.2, further six blows shall be struck varying the angle of delivery ta bring as much as possible of the periphery of the striking face or pein into contact with the normalized steel bar. 15.2.2 After each of the tests specified in 15.2 and 15.2.1, the hammer head shall show no flaw or defect. Further th,e hammer head shall still be firmly fixed to the handle and the handle shall not be damaged.

EXPLANATORY
This dimensional

NOTE
and to specify the

In order to rationalize the weights standard was issued in 1957. and other requirements in metric units, it was first revised in 1968.

In this second revision, the title of the specification has been amended to cover particularly the steel type of hammers. It is proposed to cover other types of hammers like nylon, copper and The other particulars included in this revision are soundness and aluminium hammers separately. assembly tests, depth of hardness and adoption of specific eye shapes in hammer heads.
